verses.zh: 你要大声喊叫，不可止息；扬起声来，好像吹角。向我百姓说明他们的过犯；向雅各家说明他们的罪恶。
verses.en: “Shout loudly! Don’t be quiet!Yell as loudly as a trumpet!Confront my people with their rebellious deeds;[NOTE:1] confront Jacob’s family with their sin.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “declare to my people their rebellion.”
Heb “and to the house of Jacob their sin.” The verb “declare” is understood by ellipsis (note the preceding line).

verses.zh: 他们天天寻求我，乐意明白我的道，好像行义的国民，不离弃他们　神的典章，向我求问公义的判语，喜悦亲近　神。
verses.en: They seek me day after day;they want to know my requirements,[NOTE:1] like a nation that does what is rightand does not reject the law of their God.They ask me for just decrees;they want to be near God.
notes: Heb “ways” (so KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, TEV); NLT “my laws.”

verses.zh: 他们说：我们禁食，你为何不看见呢？我们刻苦己心，你为何不理会呢？看哪，你们禁食的日子仍求利益，勒逼人为你们做苦工。
verses.en: They lament,[NOTE:1] ‘Why don’t you notice when we fast?Why don’t you pay attention when we humble ourselves?’Look, at the same time you fast, you satisfy your selfish desires,[NOTE:2] you oppress your workers.[NOTE:3]
notes: The words “they lament” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “you find pleasure”; NASB “you find your desire.”
Or perhaps, “debtors.” See HALOT 865 s.v. * עָצֵב.

verses.zh: 你们禁食，却互相争竞，以凶恶的拳头打人。你们今日禁食，不得使你们的声音听闻于上。
verses.en: Look, your fasting is accompanied by[NOTE:1] arguments, brawls,and fistfights.[NOTE:2] Do not fast as you do today,trying to make your voice heard in heaven.
notes: Heb “you fast for” (so NASB); NRSV “you fast only to quarrel.”
Heb “and for striking with a sinful fist.”

verses.zh: 这样禁食岂是我所拣选、使人刻苦己心的日子吗？岂是叫人垂头像苇子，用麻布和炉灰铺在他以下吗？你这可称为禁食、为耶和华所悦纳的日子吗？
verses.en: Is this really the kind of fasting I want?[NOTE:1] Do I want a day when people merely humble themselves,[NOTE:2] bowing their heads like a reedand stretching out[NOTE:3] on sackcloth and ashes?Is this really what you call a fast,a day that is pleasing to the Lord?
notes: Heb “choose” (so NASB, NRSV); NAB “wish.”
Heb “a day when man humbles himself.” The words “Do I want” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Or “making [their] bed.”

verses.zh: 我所拣选的禁食不是要松开凶恶的绳，解下轭上的索，使被欺压的得自由，折断一切的轭吗？
verses.en: No, this is the kind of fast I want:[NOTE:1] I want you[NOTE:2] to remove the sinful chains,to tear away the ropes of the burdensome yoke,to set free the oppressed,[NOTE:3] and to break every burdensome yoke.
notes: Heb “Is this not a fast I choose?” “No” is supplied in the translation for clarification.
The words “I want you” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “crushed.”

verses.zh: 不是要把你的饼分给饥饿的人，将飘流的穷人接到你家中，见赤身的给他衣服遮体，顾恤自己的骨肉而不掩藏吗？
verses.en: I want you[NOTE:1] to share your food with the hungryand to provide shelter for homeless, oppressed people.[NOTE:2] When you see someone naked, clothe them!Don’t turn your back on your own flesh and blood.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Is it not?” The rhetorical question here expects a positive answer, “It is!”
Heb “and afflicted [ones], homeless [ones] you should bring [into] a house.” On the meaning of מְרוּדִים (merudim, “homeless”) see HALOT 633 s.v. *מָרוּד.
Heb “and from your flesh do not hide yourself.”

verses.zh: 这样，你的光就必发现如早晨的光；你所得的医治要速速发明。你的公义必在你前面行；耶和华的荣光必作你的后盾。
verses.en: Then your light will shine like the sunrise;[NOTE:1] your restoration will quickly arrive;[NOTE:2] your godly behavior[NOTE:3] will go before you,and the Lord’s splendor will be your rear guard.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “will burst out like the dawn.” sn Light here symbolizes God’s favor and restored blessing, as the immediately following context makes clear.
Heb “prosper”; KJV “spring forth speedily.”
Or “righteousness.” Their godly behavior will be on display for all to see.
The nation will experience God’s protective presence.

verses.zh: 那时你求告，耶和华必应允；你呼求，他必说：我在这里。你若从你中间除掉重轭和指摘人的指头，并发恶言的事，
verses.en: Then you will call out, and the Lord will respond;you will cry out, and he will reply, ‘Here I am.’You must[NOTE:1] remove the burdensome yoke from among youand stop pointing fingers and speaking sinfully.
notes: Heb “if you.” In the Hebrew text vv. 9b-10 are one long conditional sentence. The protasis (multiple “if” clauses here) appears in vv. 9b-10a, with the apodosis (“then” clause) appearing in v. 10b.

verses.zh: 你心若向饥饿的人发怜悯，使困苦的人得满足，你的光就必在黑暗中发现；你的幽暗必变如正午。
verses.en: You must[NOTE:1] actively help the hungryand feed the oppressed.[NOTE:2] Then your light will dispel the darkness,[NOTE:3] and your darkness will be transformed into noonday.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “if you.” See the note on “you must” in v. 9b.
Heb “If you furnish for the hungry [with] your being, and the appetite of the oppressed you satisfy.”
Heb “will rise in the darkness.”
Heb “and your darkness [will be] like noonday.”

verses.zh: 耶和华也必时常引导你，在干旱之地使你心满意足，骨头强壮。你必像浇灌的园子，又像水流不绝的泉源。
verses.en: The Lord will continually lead you;he will feed you even in parched regions.[NOTE:1] He will give you renewed strength,[NOTE:2] and you will be like a well-watered garden,like a spring that continually produces water.
notes: Heb “he will satisfy in parched regions your appetite.”
Heb “and your bones he will strengthen.”

verses.zh: 那些出于你的人必修造久已荒废之处；你要建立拆毁累代的根基。你必称为补破口的，和重修路径与人居住的。
verses.en: Your perpetual ruins will be rebuilt;[NOTE:1] you will reestablish the ancient foundations.You will be called, ‘The one who repairs broken walls,the one who makes the streets inhabitable again.’[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and they will build from you ancient ruins.”

The Hebrew text has “the one who restores paths for dwelling.” The idea of “paths to dwell in” is not a common notion. Some have proposed emending נְתִיבוֹת (netivot, “paths”) to נְתִיצוֹת (netitsot, “ruins”), a passive participle from נָתַץ (natats, “tear down”; see HALOT 732 s.v. *נְתִיצָה), because tighter parallelism with the preceding line is achieved. However, none of the textual sources support this emendation. The line may mean that paths must be repaired in order to dwell in the land.

verses.zh: 你若在安息日掉转（或译：谨慎）你的脚步，在我圣日不以操作为喜乐，称安息日为可喜乐的，称耶和华的圣日为可尊重的；而且尊敬这日，不办自己的私事，不随自己的私意，不说自己的私话，
verses.en: You must[NOTE:1] observe the Sabbath[NOTE:2] rather than doing anything you please on my holy day.[NOTE:3] You must look forward to the Sabbath[NOTE:4] and treat the Lord’s holy day with respect.[NOTE:5] You must treat it with respect by refraining from your normal activitiesand by refraining from your selfish pursuits and from making business deals.[NOTE:6]
notes: Lit., “if you.” In the Hebrew text vv. 13-14 are one long conditional sentence. The protasis (multiple “if” clauses here) appears in v. 13, with the apodosis (“then” clause) appearing in v. 14.
Heb “if you turn from the Sabbath your feet.”
Heb “[from] doing your desires on my holy day.” The Qumran scroll 1QIsaa supplies the preposition מִן (min) on “doing.”
Heb “and call the Sabbath a pleasure”; KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV “a delight.”
Heb “and [call] the holy [day] of the Lord honored.” On קָדוֹשׁ (qadosh, “holy”) as indicating a time period, see BDB 872 s.v. 2.e (cf. also Neh 8:9-11).

Heb “and you honor it [by refraining] from accomplishing your ways, from finding your desire and speaking a word.” It is unlikely that the last phrase (“speaking a word”) is a prohibition against talking on the Sabbath; instead it probably refers to making transactions or plans (see Hos 10:4). Some see here a reference to idle talk (cf. 2 Sam 19:29).

verses.zh: 你就以耶和华为乐。耶和华要使你乘驾地的高处，又以你祖雅各的产业养育你。这是耶和华亲口说的。
verses.en: Then you will find joy in your relationship to the Lord,[NOTE:1] and I will give you great prosperity,[NOTE:2] and cause crops to grow on the land I gave to your ancestor Jacob.”[NOTE:3] Know for certain that the Lord has spoken.[NOTE:4]
notes: For a parallel use of the phrase “find joy in” (Hitpael of עָנַג [ʿanag] followed by the preposition עַל [ʿal]), see Ps 37:4.
Heb “and I will cause you to ride upon the heights of the land.” The statement seems to be an allusion to Deut 32:13, where it is associated, as here, with God’s abundant provision of food.

Heb “and I will cause you to eat the inheritance of Jacob your father.” The Hebrew term נַחֲלָה (nakhalah) likely stands by metonymy for the crops that grow on Jacob’s “inheritance” (i.e., the land he inherited as a result of God’s promise).

Heb “for the mouth of the Lord has spoken.” The introductory כִּי (ki) may be asseverative (as reflected in the translation) or causal/explanatory, explaining why the preceding promise will become reality (because it is guaranteed by the divine word).

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

BACKGROUND

- This chapter is a condemnation of religious ritual without personal faith (cf. Isa. 29:13; Jeremiah 7).

- This is the spiritual problem that caused the Exile, and in my opinion, the fall of Jerusalem in A.D. 70.
See my exegetical notes on the Olivet Discourse online (i.e. Matthew 24; Mark 13; Luke 17; 21).

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 58:1-12

1"Cry loudly, do not hold back;

Raise your voice like a trumpet,

And declare to My people their transgression

And to the house of Jacob their sins.

2Yet they seek Me day by day and delight to know My ways,

As a nation that has done righteousness

And has not forsaken the ordinance of their God.

They ask Me for just decisions,

They delight in the nearness of God.

3'Why have we fasted and You do not see?

Why have we humbled ourselves and You do not notice?'

Behold, on the day of your fast you find your desire,

And drive hard all your workers.

4Behold, you fast for contention and strife and to strike with a wicked fist.

You do not fast like you do today to make your voice heard on high.

5Is it a fast like this which I choose, a day for a man to humble himself?

Is it for bowing one's head like a reed

And for spreading out sackcloth and ashes as a bed?

Will you call this a fast, even an acceptable day to the Lord?

6Is this not the fast which I choose,

To loosen the bonds of wickedness,

To undo the bands of the yoke,

And to let the oppressed go free

And break every yoke?

7Is it not to divide your bread with the hungry

And bring the homeless poor into the house;

When you see the naked, to cover him;

And not to hide yourself from your own flesh?

8Then your light will break out like the dawn,

And your recovery will speedily spring forth;

And your righteousness will go before you;

The glory of the Lord will be your rear guard.

9Then you will call, and the Lord will answer;

You will cry, and He will say, 'Here I am.'

If you remove the yoke from your midst,

The pointing of the finger and speaking wickedness,

10And if you give yourself to the hungry

And satisfy the desire of the afflicted,

Then your light will rise in darkness

And your gloom will become like midday.

11And the Lord will continually guide you,

And satisfy your desire in scorched places,

And give strength to your bones;

And you will be like a watered garden,

And like a spring of water whose waters do not fail.

12Those from among you will rebuild the ancient ruins;

You will raise up the age-old foundations;

And you will be called the repairer of the breach,

The restorer of the streets in which to dwell.

58:1 This chapter, like many chapters in Isaiah (i.e. a typical literary marker for a new poem),
starts with a series of IMPERATIVES. The questions of interpretation are:

- who is the speaker?

- who is the recipient?

Here is the list of what is commanded (note the parallelism):

- cry loudly ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE, BDB 894, KB 1128

- do not hold back ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 362, KB 359, used in a JUSSIVE sense

- raise your voice ‒ Hiphil IMPERATIVE, BDB 926. KB 1202

- declare ‒ Hiphil IMPERATIVE, BDB 616, KB 665

The speaker is YHWH by the mouth of His prophet and the recipients are:

- pre-exilic Israel/Judah

- exilic Israel/Judah

- returning Judah

- eschatological people of God (i.e. believers, both Jew and Gentile, cf. Rom. 2:28-29; Gal. 3:7-9,29;
6:16; Eph. 2:11-3:13)

▣ "trumpet" This is BDB 1051 and denotes the prophet raising his voice like a trumpet so all
could hear YHWH's message. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: HORNS USED BY ISRAEL

▣ "their transgression. . .their sins" Formal ritual had replaced personal righteousness. They were
religious but far from YHWH (cf. Isa. 29:13-14; Jer. 7; 2 Tim. 3:5; Titus 1:16). Religion can be a barrier to true personal faith!

58:2 Notice how the false faith is characterized.

- They seek Me day by day (see SPECIAL TOPIC: Seek The Lord).

- They delight to know My ways.

- A nation. . .has not forsaken the ordinance (BDB 1048) of their God (see SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR
GOD'S REVELATION, II. F) .

- They ask Me for just decisions.

- They delight in the nearness of God.

All of this sounds great but it was a show, a farce, a religious game; words, not deeds (cf. Isa. 29:13; Jer. 7).

▣ "As a nation that has done righteousness" This is sarcasm.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "ask Me for just decisions" This refers to ways to know God's will.

- the Urim and Thummim (i.e. the High Priest, cf. Exod. 28:30; Num. 27:23; Deut. 33:8; Neh. 7:65

- the prophets (covenant mediators)

- local Levites (teachers of the application of Mosaic laws)

SPECIAL TOPIC: URIM AND THUMMIM

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

58:3 "fasted. . .humbled ourselves" The word "fasted" (Qal PERFECT, BDB 847, KB 1012)
parallels "humbled" (Piel PERFECT, BDB 776, KB 853, cf. Lev. 16:29,31). They thought God
must bless their religious acts. The OT has only one fast a year (Leviticus 16), the Day of Atonement (cf. Isa. 58:6a).
During the Exile the Jews had multiplied this to four fast days to commemorate tragic events in their national life
(i.e. the fall of Jerusalem, the destruction of the Temple, etc., cf. Zech. 7:3,5; 8:19).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FASTING

▣ "on the day of your fast you find your desire

And drive hard all your workers" They fasted for "religious" reasons and would
not allow their laborers off to participate! The effects of the Fall continue!

58:4 The fast days produced irritation not faith.

▣

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA
"to strike with a wicked fist"

AB
"strike the poor with the fist"

LXX
"strike a humble person with your fists"

Peshitta
"to strike violently with the fists

of wickedness"

NJB
"to strike viciously with your fist"

The MT has "to hit with fist wicked," but notice how the LXX takes a clue from Isa. 58:3c-d.

▣ "to make your voice heard on high" One purpose of fasting was to help with prayers, but it
caused the opposite reaction (cf. Isa. 1:15; 59:2).

58:5 This is a list of outward signs of mourning, like sackcloth and ashes, but in reality these
were only for show (cf. Matt. 6:5,16-18).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

58:6-7 "Is this not the fast which I chose" God lists what He really wants from His people
(i.e. daily social justice, cf. Exod. 21:2; Lev. 25:39-41; Deut. 15:12; and Jer. 34:8-11, which refers to
the year of Jubilee; Titus 1:16).

- to loosen the bonds of wickedness ‒ Piel INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE, BDB 834, KB 986

- to undo the bonds of the yoke ‒ Hiphil INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE, BDB 684, KB 736

- to let the oppressed go free ‒ Piel INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE, BDB 1018, KB 1511

- to break every yoke ‒ Piel PASSIVE PARTICIPLE, BDB 954, KB 1285 (i.e. indentured servitude)

- to divide your bread with the hungry ‒ Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE, BDB 828, KB 969

- to bring the homeless poor into the house ‒ Hiphil IMPERFECT, BDB 97, KB 112,
cf. Matt. 25:35; Rom. 12:13; 1 Tim. 3:2; Titus 1:8; Heb. 13:2; 1 Pet. 4:9

- to cover the naked ‒ Piel PERFECT with waw, BDB 491, KB 487, cf. James 2:14-18

- not to hide yourself from your own flesh ‒ Hithpael PERFECT, BDB 761, KB 834, cf. 1 Tim. 5:8 (i.e. help your relatives)

This is the origin of the glorified Messiah's criteria for dividing the sheep (faithful believers)
from the goats (unbelievers who act selfishly) in Matt. 25:31-46. This is not a works-righteousness, but lifestyle
evidence that the results of the Fall (i.e. self) have been reversed (i.e. others).

58:8-9b This is the promised restoration if they will repent and exhibit lifestyle faith. Notice what
true faithfulness brings.

- your light will break out like the dawn

- your recovery will speedily spring forth

- your righteousness will go before you

- the glory of the Lord will be your rear guard

- you will call and the Lord will answer

- you will cry, and He will say "Here I am" (cf. Isa. 65:1)

This is what God wanted to do for His people, but their sin and rebellion caused judgment and separation!

▣ "the glory of the Lord will be your rear guard" This refers to the
Shekinah cloud of glory being their protection as it was during the Exodus period (cf. Exod. 14:19 and Isa. 52:12).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (OT)

58:9a,b These lines of poetry emphasize YHWH's availability to an obedient covenant people.

- He will hear their prayers

- He will be available (i.e. "Here I am," cf. Isa. 6:8)

58:9c-10 "If" This (cf. Isa. 58:9 and 10) shows the conditional element of God's reciprocal
covenantal relationship ("if. . .then," often assumed but not stated) with His people. Note the conditions.

- remove the yoke (i.e. indentured servants/slaves)

- stop the pointing of the finger, cf. Prov. 6:13

- stop speaking wickedness

- give yourself to the hungry (Hiphil JUSSIVE, BDB 807, KB 920)

- satisfy the desire of the afflicted

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

58:9 "The pointing of the finger" This refers to evil gestures or words (cf. Prov. 6:13).

- formal legal accusation

- announce a curse

- social slander

58:10c-12 The "then" (blessing) part of the conditional covenant (cf. Leviticus 26;
Deuteronomy 28-29) is spelled out.

- your light will rise in darkness

- your gloom will become like midday

- the Lord will continually guide you

- the Lord will satisfy your desire

- the Lord will give strength to your bones

- you will be like a watered garden

- you will be like a spring of water whose waters do not fail

- you will rebuild the ancient ruins

- you will raise up the age old foundations

- you will be called the repairer of the breach

- you will be called the restorer of the streets

The prophet uses several sources of imagery to describe YHWH's presence and blessing.

- light vs. darkness

- shepherd imagery

- agricultural blessing

- rebuilding imagery

58:11 There are two textual issues in this verse.

- Isa. 58:11b

The word "desire" is nephesh (BDB 659) which has many connotations (see SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH).

The "scorched places" is found only here (BDB 850, KB 1019) and the meaning is uncertain.

- Isa. 58:11e

NASB, NKJV
"whose waters do not fail"

The MT's VERB (BDB 469, KB 467, Piel IMPERFECT) means "to lie"
or "to deceive." The sense seems to be "the waters God provides; they never 'lie' or 'deceive'" (i.e. always flows [NJB])

58:12 YHWH promises that the returnees from exile will rebuild their land, but this seems to contradict
Isa. 32:14 (as well as Jer. 25:9). There are two issues here.

- the eastern peoples' use of hyperbole (see SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE)

- the ambiguity of the Bible's use of "forever," "everlasting" (see SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

Prophecies were meant to effect change in the way God's people were living. If they did
not change, the prophecies were sure! However, if repentance and rightoues living occurred, the prophecies were canceled (i.e. Jonah)!

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 58:13-14

13"If because of the sabbath, you turn your foot

From doing your own pleasure on My holy day,

And call the sabbath a delight, the holy day of the Lord honorable,

And honor it, desisting from your own ways,

From seeking your own pleasure

And speaking your own word,

14Then you will take delight in the Lord ,

And I will make you ride on the heights of the earth;

And I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob your father,

For the mouth of the Lord has spoken."

58:13-14 This strophe uses obedience to the Sabbath requirements as a way to know a person's
attitude and faithfulness.

- turn your foot from doing your own pleasure, to YHWH's sabbath (cf. Isa. 58:13)

- delight in the sabbath by calling it "honorable" (BDB 457, KB 455, is used twice in Isa. 58:13)

Notice again the conditional covenant ("if. . .then"). The benefits are listed in Isa. 58:14b,c.

58:13 "the sabbath" See Exodus 20:8-11 and Isaiah 56.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SABBATH

58:14 "For the mouth of the Lord has spoken" This expresses the trustworthiness and power of
God's promises (cf. Genesis 1; Isa. 55:11)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

58:14b "I will make you ride on the heights of the earth" There are two interpretive issues.

- meaning of the VERB "ride on the heights"

- imagery for military victory and security (i.e. cities, forts built on hills)

- imagery of God-given abundance (cf. Deut. 32:13-14), v. 14c

- "the earth" (see SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH)

- Palestine/Canaan

- universal implications for a new day of YHWH's blessing on the planet

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What is the difference between biblical faith and religiosity?

- How is ethics related to theology?

- What is the purpose of fasting?

- What is the purpose of the Sabbath? Is it valid in our day?
